source_text:
καὶ οὐχὶ δὴ πάντως τελειοῦντος εἰς ἁγιασμὸν τοῦ νόμου.
{ΠΑΛΛ.} Εὖ ἔφης.
{ΚΥΡ.} Οὐκοῦν τὴν τοῦ Ἰσραὴλ κλῆσιν ὑποσημαίνοντες, ὡς ἐν ὑπερτάτοις τε καὶ μέσοις, καὶ τοῖς ἔτι μείοσι, μόσχοι τε καὶ κριοὶ, καὶ μὴν καὶ ἀμνοὶ κατεθύοντο τῷ Θεῷ, καὶ ἐν ἐλάττοσιν ἀεὶ τῶν μόσχων ὁ ἀριθμὸς, ὡς ἐκλειπόντων ἀεὶ τῶν ἐξειλεγμένων καὶ τῶν ἐν ὑπεροχαῖς, καὶ δοκιμωτάτων, τὴν σπάνιν νοσοῦντος ἀεὶ τοῦ καιροῦ, καὶ μέχρι τῆς ἑβδόμης, τοῦτ' ἔστι, τῆς τοῦ Σωτῆρος ἡμῶν ἐπιδημίας, καθ' ὂν ὁ σαββατισμὸς ἐν πνεύματι, καὶ κατάληξις ἔργων τῶν εἰς ἁμαρτίαν ἀνέφυ λοιπόν. Δεδικαιώμεθα γὰρ ἐν Χριστῷ, καταῤῥέοντος ἤδη πρὸς τέλος τοῦ παρόντος αἰῶνος. Σημεῖον δ' ἂν γένοιτο καὶ τοῦδε πάλιν, τῆς ὅλης ἡμῖν ἑβδομάδος ὡς ἐν ἐσχάτοις τὸ Σάββατον κείμενον. Ταύτῃτοι σοφῶς ἵστησι μὲν ὁ νόμος φησὶ μέχρι τοῦ Σαββάτου τῶν ἀρχαίων θυμάτων τὴν προσκομιδὴν, τοῦτ' ἔστι, τὴν ἐν νόμῳ κλῆσιν, καὶ τὴν κατ' αὐτὸν ἱερουργίαν, ἀντεισφέρει δὲ ὥσπερ τὴν ἐν Χριστῷ λέγων· «Καὶ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τῇ ὀγδόῃ, ἐξόδιον ἔσται ὑμῖν. Πᾶν ἔργον λατρευτὸν οὐ ποιήσετε ἐν αὐτῇ, καὶ προσάξετε ὁλοκαύτωμα κάρπωμα εἰς ὀσμὴν εὐωδίας τῷ Κυρίῳ μόσχον ἕνα, κριὸν ἕνα, ἀμνοὺς ἐνιαυσίους ἑπτὰ ἀμώμους. Αἱ θυσίαι αὐτῶν καὶ αἱ σπονδαὶ αὐτῶν τῷ μόσχῳ καὶ τῷ κριῷ καὶ τοῖς ἀμνοῖς κατὰ ἀριθμὸν αὐτῶν, κατὰ τὴν σύγκρισιν αὐτῶν, καὶ χίμαρον ἐξ αἰγῶν ἕνα περὶ ἁμαρτίας· πλὴν τῆς ὁλοκαυτώσεως τῆς διὰ παντός. Αἱ θυσίαι αὐτῶν καὶ αἱ σπονδαὶ αὐτῶν· ταῦτα ποιήσετε Κυρίῳ ἐν ταῖς ἑορταῖς ὑμῶν, πλὴν τῶν εὐχῶν ὑμῶν, καὶ τὰ ἑκούσια ὑμῶν, καὶ τὰ ὁλοκαυτώματα ὑμῶν, καὶ τὰς θυσίας ὑμῶν, καὶ τὰς σπονδὰς ὑμῶν, καὶ τὰ σωτήρια ὑμῶν.» Ἀκούεις τοῦ νόμου λέγοντος ἐναργῶς· «Ἐξόδιόν ἐστιν;» Ἐκβέβηκε γὰρ ἡ ὡς ἐν σκιαῖς λατρεία, καὶ ἡ ἐν τύπῳ παίδευσις, κατὰ τὴν ὀγδόην, καθ' ἢν ἀνεβίω Χριστὸς, καὶ τῆς ἐν πνεύματι περιτομῆς εἰσπέπαικεν ὁ καιρός. Ἐξεκλείσθη μὲν γὰρ ἡ ἀρχαία τῶν κεκλημένων πληθὺς, ἔγκλημα νοσοῦσα τὴν ἀπιστίαν, ἀντανέφυ δὲ ὥσπερ λαὸς ὁ νέος, καὶ διαπρέπων μὲν ἰσχύϊ πνευματικῇ, τοῦτο γὰρ ὁ μόσχος, εὐδοκιμῶν δὲ τελείως, ὡς ἐν ἡλικίας πληρώματι, τοῦτο γὰρ ὁ κριὸς, τῆς δὲ ἐν Χριστῷ νηπιότητος καὶ ἀκακίας τὸ ἐξαίρετον κάλλος, τοῦτο γὰρ ὁ ἀμνὸς, εἰ καὶ ἐν πληθύϊ νοοῖτο τῇ τελειοτάτῃ. Τὸ γὰρ εἶναι λέγειν ἑπτὰ τοὺς ἀμνοὺς, τοῦτό που πάντως ὑποδηλοῖ. Ἕπεται γὰρ καὶ ὁ χίμαρος. Ἐν Χριστῷ γὰρ εὐδοκιμεῖ διὰ πίστεως, εἰς ὀσμὴν εὐωδίας ἀναβαίνων τῷ Θεῷ, καθὰ πολλάκις εἰρήκαμεν.
{ΠΑΛΛ.} Ὧδε ἔχει.
{ΚΥΡ.} Ὅτι δὲ σαββατιοῦμεν ἐν Χριστῷ, καταλύοντες εἰς ἀνάπαυσιν, διά γε τοῦ δεῖν σπουδασμάτων ἡμᾶς καταλῆξαι κοσμικῶν καὶ γεωδεστέρας φροντίδος οὐκ ἀνεχομένους ἔτι, κατατρυφῶντας δὲ μᾶλλον τοῦ Κυρίου, καθὰ γέγραπται, καὶ κλῆρον ἔχοντας παρ' αὐτῷ τὸν ἐξαίρετον, σαφηνιεῖ λέγων ἐν
pass_a_gloss: (most approved in obedience to God,) and the law not at all perfecting into sanctification. PALL.: You spoke well. CYR.: So, signifying the calling of Israel, as in highest and middle and those still lesser, both calves and rams and also lambs were sacrificed to God, and the number of the calves always in fewer, as the chosen and those in superiorities and most approved always failing, the time always being sick with the scarcity, and until the seventh, that is, the sojourn of our Savior, in which the sabbath-keeping in spirit and cessation of works toward sin sprang up at last. For we have been justified in Christ, the present age already flowing down toward its end. And a sign of this too again would be the Sabbath of the whole week lying for us as in last things. Therefore wisely the law, it says, stops until the Sabbath the bringing of the ancient victims, that is, the calling in law, and the sacred service according to it, and brings in as it were in exchange the one in Christ, saying: 'And on the eighth day, a closing (exodion) will be for you. Every work of service you will not do on it, and you will bring a whole burnt offering, an offering for an odor of fragrance to the Lord, one calf, one ram, lambs a year old seven unblemished. Their sacrifices and their libations for the calf and the ram and the lambs according to their number, according to their comparison (rule), and one he-goat from goats concerning sin, besides the whole burnt offering throughout all. Their sacrifices and their libations; these you will do to the Lord in your feasts, besides your vows, and your voluntary things, and your whole burnt offerings, and your sacrifices, and your libations, and your salvation-offerings.' Do you hear the law saying plainly: 'It is a closing'? For the worship as in shadows and the training in type has gone out, on the eighth, on which Christ came back to life, and the time of the circumcision in spirit burst in. For the ancient multitude of the called was shut out, sick with the charge of unbelief, and in exchange there sprang up as it were the new people, and excelling in spiritual strength, for this is the calf, and approved perfectly, as in fullness of age, for this is the ram, and the choice beauty of the infancy and innocence in Christ, for this is the lamb, even if it be understood in the most perfect multitude. For to say that the lambs are seven surely hints this. For the he-goat also follows. For in Christ it is approved through faith, going up for an odor of fragrance to God, as we have often said. PALL.: So it holds. CYR.: And that we will keep Sabbath in Christ, putting up for rest, through our needing to cease from worldly pursuits and not enduring any longer more earthy care, but rather delighting in the Lord, as it is written, and having with him the choice lot, he will make clear saying in (continues).
pass_b_english: Cyril: …though the law did not at all bring them to perfection in sanctification.

Cyril: So calves and rams and lambs were sacrificed to God, signifying the calling of Israel, as in the highest, the middle, and those still lesser. And the number of the calves kept growing smaller, since the chosen, the outstanding and the most approved kept failing, as the times kept suffering from their scarcity, up to the seventh day, that is, the coming of our Savior, in which at last the sabbath-keeping in the spirit, and rest from works that lead to sin, sprang up. For we have been justified in Christ, as the present age already flows down toward its end. And this would again be a sign of it, that for us the sabbath lies at the end of the whole week. That is why, it says, the law wisely stops the bringing of the ancient victims at the sabbath, that is, the calling under the law and the service according to it, and brings in, as it were, in its place the calling in Christ, saying: ‘And on the eighth day there shall be a closing festival for you. You shall do no work of service on it, and you shall bring a whole burnt offering, an offering for a fragrant aroma to the Lord: one calf, one ram, seven unblemished lambs a year old. Their sacrifices and their drink offerings for the calf and the ram and the lambs, according to their number, according to their rule; and one male goat from the goats for sin, besides the continual whole burnt offering. Their sacrifices and their drink offerings: these you shall offer to the Lord at your feasts, besides your vows, and your freewill offerings, and your whole burnt offerings, and your sacrifices, and your drink offerings, and your offerings of salvation’ (Numbers 29:35–39).

Do you hear the law saying plainly, ‘It is a closing festival’? For the worship in shadows and the training in type came to their close on the eighth day, on which Christ came back to life, and the time of circumcision in the spirit (Romans 2:29) broke in. The ancient multitude of those who had been called was shut out, sick with the charge of unbelief, and in its place there sprang up, as it were, the new people: excelling in spiritual strength, and that is the calf; perfectly approved, as in the fullness of maturity, and that is the ram; and having the choice beauty of the childlikeness and innocence that is in Christ, and that is the lamb, even if it is understood as in the most perfect multitude; for saying that the lambs are seven surely hints at this. And the goat follows too. For it is in Christ that the people is approved through faith, as it goes up to God as a fragrant aroma, as we have often said.

Cyril: That we shall keep sabbath in Christ, coming to rest, in that we must cease from worldly pursuits and no longer bear earthly care, but rather delight in the Lord, as it is written (Psalm 37:4), and have with him the choice inheritance, he will make clear when he says in…

choices.english: a closing festival ... came to their close
choices.why: Cyril plays on ἐξόδιον (closing, going out) with ἐκβέβηκε (has gone out); English keeps the close/closing link.

choices.english: it is in Christ that the people is approved
choices.why: The subject is the new people of the preceding sentence; named for clarity.
